timeline.title: Osmosis - Wikipedia
lines: Osmosis is the net movement of solvent molecules through a selectively permeable membrane.
The solvent moves from a region of lower solute concentration to a region of higher solute concentration.
It tends to equalise the solute concentrations on the two sides of the membrane.
Osmotic pressure is the external pressure needed to stop this net flow of solvent.
Osmotic pressure is the external pressure needed to stop this net flow of solvent.
The membrane lets solvent molecules pass but blocks most solute particles.
On the side with more solute, fewer solvent molecules are free to cross back.
The result is a net flow of solvent toward the more concentrated solution.

Osmotic pressure depends on the number of dissolved particles, not on their identity.
For dilute solutions the van 't Hoff equation gives Π = iMRT.
Here i is the van 't Hoff factor, M the molarity, R the gas constant and T the temperature.

Plant cells rely on osmosis to stay turgid: water enters the vacuole and presses on the cell wall.
Red blood cells in a hypotonic solution swell and may burst (haemolysis).
In a hypertonic solution the same cells lose water and shrink (crenation).
Isotonic solutions cause no net movement of water across the membrane.
